name: Picture in Picture (video)
plain: Pops a video into a small always-on-top window, usually after a click.
meaning: A site can float a video above all other apps, which keeps attention on its content while the person works elsewhere. The person can close or resize it, and a site cannot place or hide the window.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.persistence: Ends on exit, video unload or navigation; nothing is stored
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes need allow="picture-in-picture" (Permissions Policy picture-in-picture, default self)
steps: Browser opens a floating window with the video
Page can listen to enterpictureinpicture and leavepictureinpicture

limits.headline: Can pop a video into a small floating window after you tap
limits.user_action: You tap the Picture in Picture button on a video.
can: Move a video into a small always-on-top window
Keep it playing while you use other tabs or apps
Return it to the page when you ask
cannot: Start without a click, tap or keypress
Float anything other than a video
Keep the video playing after you close the floating window

story.what_it_is: Pops a video into a small always on top window, usually after you click.

marketing.name: Picture-in-Picture API
marketing.pitch: Explains how a video can float in a small window above other apps so people can keep watching.

story.for_you: You click a button on a video and it floats in a small window. You can then read a different page or work in another app while it plays.
story.for_makers: It helps a site keep people watching. A video that floats is a video that keeps getting watched, which matters for ads and subscriptions.

use_cases.example: You pop a lecture or recipe video out and keep it above your notes.
A live sports or news stream floats in the corner while you answer emails.
A streaming site lets you watch a show in a corner window while you scroll.
A browser game stream floats over a walkthrough or guide page.
A course video floats next to a coding tab so students can follow along.
A news site floats a small video player that follows you down the page, with an ad before the clip.
A video call app lets you float the other person while you take notes.

technical_bounds: Needs user activation to enter, but leaving can happen any time
Video only (document PiP is a separate API and Chromium or Firefox only)
The element needs metadata loaded and must not carry the disablePictureInPicture attribute
Window size and place are chosen by the browser; the site gets width and height through PictureInPictureWindow and a resize event
Safari before 13.1 used its own webkitSetPresentationMode; standard API from Safari 13.1 (BCD)
Chrome for Android has the API from Chrome 105

abuse: Persisting a distraction or an ad over other apps

history.change: Picture in Picture Web API ships on desktop
Standard PiP API for macOS Safari
requestPictureInPicture API arrives (BCD), after Firefox's own PiP toggle
